title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Add a reusable Terraform module (modules/vpc-control-plane) and installer integration to provision a multi-AZ control plane VPC for private deployments. This includes AZ-aware private subnets, interface endpoints (S3, STS, KMS, ECR, SSM), hardened security groups scoped to control-plane CIDRs, cross-account VPC peering helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone configuration with conditional forwarding for customer VPC name resolution. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private need a repeatable, secure network footprint that integrates with customer VPCs and supports private DNS resolution. Prior iterations required manual steps and ad-hoc scripts; this module standardizes defaults and exposes knobs for advanced environments. What changed: added terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane with main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf and example usage; implemented interface endpoint submodule and security-group templates; added route53 submodule that creates a private hosted zone and optional outbound resolver rules for Route53 Resolver forwarding; installer integration changes under install/terraform to wire module outputs into the private control plane installer; updated helm values placeholder that the installer uses for control plane CIDRs and route53 zone IDs. Migration & upgrade notes: module is opt-in by default; existing customers are not automatically migrated. For upgrades, there is an upgrade plan in docs/upgrade-control-plane.md describing a staged apply (create new subnets in spare AZs, migrate ENIs/services, then decommission old subnets) and a rollback recipe using terraform state snapshots. Security considerations: default SGs are deny-all except explicit control-plane management ports between subnets and customer-peered CIDRs; KMS and ECR endpoints are interface endpoints to avoid internet egress. Testing: unit/module tests with kitchen-terraform and a full end-to-end run in the QA account with three AZs and a simulated customer-peering VPC. CI: plan/apply run is gated behind a terraform workspace check; CI initially failed due to missing IAM policy for resolver but passed after fix and rerun. Checklist: [x] module tests, [x] integration test in QA, [x] security review completed, [x] docs/upgrade-control-plane.md added, [x] Linear ENG-4123 linked. Related: linear/ENG-4123, ops/OPS-118, support/SUP-9821. Reference design: https://docs.internal.redwood/vpc-control-plane-design. Notes: reviewers flagged Route53 TTLs and resolver rule ownership edge cases — addressed by making forwarding optional and documenting cross-account delegation; SG rules tightened per Priya's suggestion.

release_notes: Add terraform module for provisioning a multi-AZ control plane VPC with private subnets, interface endpoints, hardened security groups, optional cross-account peering helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone + optional forwarding. Includes upgrade and rollback guidance for staged migrations. (opt-in)
testing_summary: Module unit tests (kitchen-terraform) and end-to-end deploy ran in QA account (3 AZ). Tests validated subnet allocations, interface endpoints presence, SG rules, and resolver forwarding behavior. CI plan initially failed due to resolver IAM role; rerun succeeded.
notes: This change is opt-in; operators must set `enable_control_plane_provisioning=true` in installer vars. Keep an eye on Route53 cross-account delegation; we added explicit instructions and an example with CloudFormation delegation role.
